venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

editor_test.pain_point: Dependent events, evolving catalogue state, and unquantified score differences can produce invalid classifier comparisons.
editor_test.goal: Determine whether candidate severe felt-intensity classifiers comply with predefined comparison rules and whether apparent improvements remain supported.
editor_test.intended_user: Applied-ML engineers, benchmark maintainers, and reviewers.
editor_test.decision_enabled: Admit an in-contract candidate and decide whether its Brier improvement over a declared reference is supported or unresolved.
editor_test.error_prevented: Out-of-contract comparisons and false winner declarations.
editor_test.substantive_result: Four learned baselines improve over no-skill; adding depth clearly improves on magnitude alone; logistic regression and XGBoost both round to Brier 0.181 and remain unresolved in their paired comparison.
editor_test.non_use_boundary: Public labels preclude untouched confirmation; the work is not real-time warning or operational triage.
editor_test.verbatim_paraphrase: The benchmark gives engineers a fair retrospective test and a transparent logistic reference that more complex methods must improve on; confirmation still requires fresh hidden data.

independent_reader_paraphrases: A fixed DYFI benchmark admits candidates by schema and role rules and supports superiority only with paired Brier uncertainty.
All four learned models beat constant prevalence, depth improves on magnitude alone, and logistic regression and XGBoost remain unresolved at the leading rounded score.
Engineers can use the benchmark to reject invalid comparisons and test whether a more complex method really improves on a simple transparent reference.

venue_constraint_blocker: JEAS is fully open access rather than hybrid; user must explicitly relax the hybrid requirement or select another venue.
